case_name: State of Uttar Pradesh v Rama Kant and Others
facts: The Judgment was delivered by : Arijit Pasayat, J.
Heard learned counsel for the State and learned counsel for the respondents.
The occurrence took place on 23/10/1979. According to the prosecution, the eye witnesses were PW.1, the complainant, PW.4-the mother and PW.5 the wife of the complainant.
Though PW.3 was examined as alleged eye witness, he did not support the prosecution version.
The defence version was that it was PW.1 who was responsible for causing death of the deceased who happened to be his brother.
In appeal the stand taken was that the presence of PW.4 was doubtful.
In the First Information Report lodged, there was no mention about PW.1 and PW.4 having witnessed the occurrence.
According to the so-called eye witnesses, large number of injuries were caused by bricks bats and sharp edged weapons.
The medical evidence did not disclose injuries which could have been possible by sharp edged weapons and bricks.
It is to be noted that accused No.1 has died during the pendency of the appeal before the High Court.
petitioner_arguments: Evidence of the eye witnesses should not have been discarded by the High Court.
respondent_arguments: Supported the judgment of the High Court.
court_reasoning: The non-seizure of a blood stained axe belonging to PW.1 at the spot of occurrence was a highly suspicious circumstance.
The presence of informant or PW.4 has not been indicated in the First Information Report.
It was not the informant but one of the accused persons Jai Narain who had made arrangement for shifting the deceased in injured condition to the hospital.
All these circumstances certainly have relevance and the High Court has rightly placed reliance on them to hold that the accused persons were not guilty.
holding: The appeal fails and is dismissed.
The bailable warrants executed in terms of the order dated 9/2/2009 shall stand discharged.
cases_cited: State of Uttar Pradesh v Rama Kant
